title: Season 1, Ep 10: Disaster recovery for AI platforms
oneliner: Enterprise AI DR means multi-region vector databases with failover and a fallback gateway that shifts requests to a secondary LLM in another region when the first fails.
says: As an AI infrastructure architect setting up an enterprise-grade AI production environment, you must plan the disaster recovery environment. Vector databases must live in multiple regions so one region's failure fails over to another. The LLM must have a fallback gateway: when a request to the first LLM fails, it falls back to a secondary LLM running in a different region. That makes the AI infrastructure resilient.
explained: DR for AI is classic reliability engineering applied to a new stack - which is why this closes Season 1. The components are new (vector databases, model endpoints) but the questions are reel #2's: what happens when it fails, and how fast do we recover? The vector database matters as much as the model: lose your embeddings and your RAG system answers from nothing, so it must be replicated like any system of record.

The fallback gateway deserves attention because it implies something subtle: your secondary LLM may be a different model, possibly smaller or from another provider. Failover then is not just routing - it is a behavior change your applications must tolerate. That is one more reason Season 2 centralizes prompts and evaluation: a platform that tests behavior across models makes fallback safe instead of surprising.
takeaway: Replicate the vector store across regions and put a fallback LLM behind the gateway - and test that your apps behave acceptably on the secondary model.
